rules.passes: R is found in a first pass without the message-after-revocation checks; a second pass applies them with that R; the problems reported are those of the second pass. Their order here (the second pass in message order, then those of the revocation messages) is this implementation's; the draft does not fix an order
rules.applies: a revocation applies when it covers the mandate applied in the first pass (its hash is listed, or the mandate notBefore < revokedBefore) or, when no mandate is applied, when revokedBefore > 0; the site revocation counts only for an applied mandate
rules.final: Offered, Accepted or Active with R <= at is Cancelled; then Expired; a revocation never changes the state when met; a verdict is allowed whatever its issued
rules.order: messages lists the message order: offer, accept, mandate, deliver:<i>, acceptance, revocation:<i>; the verdict judges delivery `of`

cases.name: a revocation message placed before the accept, issued before it: the accept is refused, the thread is cancelled
the same revocation from the site list: the same result
a revocation message placed before the accept but issued after the delivery: where it appears does not matter
a dated revocation and a refused mandate: the dated one applies, the site list found for the refused mandate does not count
two revocations, an early and a late one: R is the early one, a delivery between them is refused
a site revocation issued after the delivery and before the verdict: the thread stays Settled
the same revocation as a message after the verdict: the same result
a revocation issued after `at`: not cancelled yet
a revocation that covers neither the mandate nor any date: revocation-mismatch, no R
cancelled and expired at once: Cancelled comes first
no revocation, past the mandate's expiry: Expired
an accept signed exactly at R is allowed (only after R is refused)
a delivery signed exactly at R is allowed, and accepted
R equal to at cancels
R one second after at does not cancel yet

rules.funded: a mandate names funds when any scope cap or feeCap is not 0, or any scope token or feeToken is not the zero address (§5.1)
rules.switch: without the switch every mandate is checked by the phase-0 rules (phase0-no-funds, subdelegate-not-allowed), exactly as in 1.8; with { enforcement: "escrow-channel" } a mandate that names funds is checked by the phase-1 static rules instead (phase 1), one that names none still by the phase-0 rules (phase 0)
rules.static: in this order: scope-token-cap-mismatch for each scope item whose token is zero and cap is not, or the other way; fee-token-cap-mismatch likewise for feeToken and feeCap; scope-duplicate-provider once for each provider named by two or more items with a non-zero cap (addresses compared in any case); mode-scope-mismatch when mode is 0 (pay) and any scope cap is not 0 or any scope token not zero; subdelegate-not-allowed. The order is this implementation's; the draft fixes none
rules.warnings: scope-includes-agent is reported, never refused, for a scope item with a cap whose provider is the agent (here; the same-holder case needs the chain); it is a static warning, reported whatever the static problems are (review p1m12 F7)
rules.nonce: a static problem keeps the nonce unrecorded (as phase0-no-funds does); recordsNonce says whether these static rules alone allow recording it
rules.planRefusals: escrowPlan refuses, in this order: the static rules; nothing-to-plan; with now, session-expired then session-too-long; with the facts read on chain (M3): holder-not-current (the plan's holder is not the principal's current holder), holder-changed-since-signing (review p1m3 recheck 3: the case's facts.signer, who signed the mandate, is given and is null or not the plan's holder), on the container path principal-not-deployed, principal-not-opened, execute-fee-too-high (executeFee above maxExecuteFee, the case's facts or else planBase's; an executeFee without maxExecuteFee is an input error, never planned, review p1m3 R1 and recheck), holder-short-of-fee (the holderBalance fact is below one executeFee, review p1m3 S4), execute-reverts (a simulated execute with the fee still reverts); with a session history, key-reused (the agent key is recorded for another mandate: an entry with another mandateHash, or one read from the logs, without a hash, that is not on one of this mandate's channels for this consumer ending at its expires); with a history and the case's facts.pinBlock (the block the facts were read at), pin-not-after-record (review p1m3 recheck 3: an entry with a block at or after pinBlock that is this mandate's, as for key-reused, with its agentKey on any channel, or that is on a channel this plan funds: same chain, the item's escrow, this consumer, the item's provider). Then each capped scope item in scope order, in this order: the agent's own container (agent-key-on-fee-channel); the plan's consumer, the holder on the holder path or the principal on the container path (provider-is-consumer); an escrow named by any entry of the plan (provider-is-escrow); a provider whose manifest names no escrow (provider-unresolvable); an escrow on no list (escrow-not-allowed); an escrow without code (escrow-other-chain); a token other than the scope item's, none, or an escrow already given with another token by an earlier item (escrow-token-mismatch); a history entry of this mandate (as for key-reused: its hash, or no hash on this consumer's channel at its expires) with its agentKey for this provider on another channel, another escrow or another consumer, that is not released (funded-elsewhere, review p1m3 recheck: a channel is released only when its consumer is the plan's, an entry for it has claimedAtPlan, and the entry's `elsewhere` fact { escrow, consumer, channel, pendingLive, claimed } for that channel says channel 0, no live request, and gives claimed; a missing fact is not released); the other funding path's channel to this provider (the principal's on the holder path, the holder's on the container path: the entry's otherPath { channel, session }) holding money or a session of the agent key (other-path-funded, review p1m3 S1); a live request (withdraw-pending); a channel above its cap (channel-exceeds-cap); the agent key with a session on the channel that is neither 0 nor the mandate's expires (key-already-authorised); the agent key's session already equal to expires (the plan was applied: the key may have spent since) and no history entry of this session (same chain, escrow, consumer, provider, key, expires; a mandateHash that is this mandate's or null) with claimedAtPlan, or no claimed fact, while the channel is below its cap, or, without such an entry, while claimed is given and not 0 (channel-spent: the baseline is never reset to today's claimedOf, review p1m3 recheck); a channel above its budget (channel-exceeds-budget): cap - spentElsewhere - spentHere, at least 0, where spentElsewhere is the sum over the released channels elsewhere of claimed - the smallest claimedAtPlan of its entries, and spentHere is claimed - the smallest claimedAtPlan of this session's entries when the session equals expires and such an entry and claimed are given (0 otherwise); a budget of 0 on a channel holding 0 where the agent key has no session (budget-exhausted, review p1m3 recheck 3: no authorizeSession alone on an empty channel); another key in the history on this channel (same chain, escrow, consumer, provider) whose session ends at or after now (channel-session-live). Last, on the container path, holder-short-of-fee again when holderBalance is below executeFee times the number of steps. The holder is the case's `holder`, else planBase.holder, on both paths (review p1m3 S6: the container path needs it too)
rules.planSession: a channel where the agent key's session already equals expires gets no authorizeSession step (it was authorised for this mandate), and is funded only up to its budget (review p1m3 B1), never back to the cap; every channel, a fresh one too, is funded to its budget - channel, the budget being cap - spentElsewhere - spentHere (see planRefusals), so for each (mandate, provider) the key's spending on every channel the history records plus what is open to it never exceeds the cap however often the plan is run (review p1m3 recheck). The plan lists in `record` one history entry per capped item { chainId, escrow, consumer, provider, key, expires, mandateHash, claimedAtPlan, spentElsewhere }: claimedAtPlan is the history entry's (carried forward, with or without the claimed fact) where the session equals expires and such an entry exists, else the claimed fact, else null; spentElsewhere is a decimal string; expect.claimedAtPlan and expect.spentElsewhere list them in scope order where a case states them. Each record entry carries block, the case's facts.pinBlock or null (expect.recordBlock lists them in scope order where a case states it). expect.checked, where a case states it, is { history, signer }: whether the case gives a history at all, and a facts.signer (an empty one [] is given; review p1m3 recheck 3: a history left out is not checked, never taken as empty)
rules.closeOut: closeOutPlan: for each capped scope item in scope order whose channel is not 0: with a live request (requestedAt != 0 and now <= requestedAt + 48 h + 7 d), a withdraw only, inside [requestedAt + 48 h, requestedAt + 48 h + 7 d], for min(requested, channel), the rest remaining; otherwise (no request, or a lapsed one) requestWithdraw(provider, channel) and a withdraw 48 h to 48 h + 7 d after it. Every requestWithdraw comes before every withdraw. Refused, in this order: on the container path holder-not-current (the current holder must send it), execute-fee-too-high (executeFee above the caller's maxExecuteFee), holder-short-of-fee (holderBalance below one executeFee) and execute-reverts (a simulated execute still reverts); consumer-unknown (review p1m3 S2: the case's history records sessions of this mandate, same chain, its agentKey, its expires and a capped provider, and none for this consumer: the holder on the holder path, the principal on the container path); escrow-unknown (an entry's escrow is null: where the money is is not known, R23); all channels empty: nothing-to-close; last, on the container path, holder-short-of-fee when holderBalance is below executeFee times the number of steps. With fullRequest (review p1m3 S5) a live request for less than the channel is replaced: state replace, requestWithdraw(provider, channel) and a withdraw timed from it. On the holder path the wallet that funded closes its own channels
rules.applied: after a plan was sent: allowance-not-zero for each escrow of the plan's checks whose allowance is not 0 (with its approve(escrow, 0)), then for each capped item channel-not-at-cap and session-not-set (the agent key's session != expires). channel-not-at-cap: when the plan's record has claimedAtPlan, channel + (claimed - claimedAtPlan) != the target (what the key spent since the plan counts, review p1m3 B1); otherwise channel != the target. The target is cap - the record's spentElsewhere, at least 0 (review p1m3 recheck). Where the record has claimedAtPlan, each channel-not-at-cap has a cause (expect.causes, in order, where a case states them): excess above the target; below it, fund-failed when the allowance read for the record's escrow is not 0, else withdrawn-or-not-sent
rules.plan: escrowPlan: per escrow one approve of exactly the sum of (cap - channel) over its capped providers, omitted when 0; then fund(provider, cap - channel) for each capped provider in scope order, omitted when 0; then authorizeSession(provider, agentKey, expires) for each; then one allowance check per escrow that had an approve. Steps list [kind, escrow, provider, amount]. On the holder path every transaction goes to the token or the escrow; on the container path to the principal (execute), with the caller's executeFee as its value, and expect.fees, where a case states it, is { perExecute: executeFee, executes: the number of steps, total: their product } (review p1m3 R1). A refusal names its reason
rules.history: sessionHistory: one entry per session (chainId, escrow, consumer, provider, key, expires, mandateHash; addresses in any case). A record of a session already kept adds no entry; its claimedAtPlan replaces the kept one only when that is null and it is not (null -> a value, never a value -> another value or null); its block replaces the kept one when that is null or lower (the latest pin; an expect row with a fourth element states the block). A log entry (mandateHash null) of a session kept with a hash adds nothing and fills nothing. expect lists [escrow, mandateHash, claimedAtPlan] for each entry in the order kept
rules.spend: spendDecision(record, request): may the agent key sign a voucher of request.cumulative for request.price to request.provider on request.escrow for request.consumer at request.now? Refused with the first that applies, in this order: spend-not-started (the record's state is not started); spend-stopped (the record has stopped); spend-other-chain (request.chainId is not the record's); spend-out-of-scope (the provider is none of the record's providers); spend-escrow-changed (the escrow is not the provider's pinned one); spend-consumer-changed (the consumer is not the record's); spend-not-yet (now before notBefore); spend-expired (now after expires); spend-bad-amount (price or cumulative 0); spend-call-price-ceiling-above-cap (request.maxPrice given and above the provider's cap); spend-call-price-ceiling-unset (no request.maxPrice and the default per-call ceiling, floor(cap * 10 / 100), is 0); spend-call-price-above-ceiling (the price above the per-call ceiling: request.maxPrice when given, otherwise floor(cap * 10 / 100)); spend-cap-exceeded (cumulative above the provider's base + cap). Addresses compare in any case. stop is true for spend-other-chain, spend-escrow-changed, spend-consumer-changed and spend-expired (they stop the order for good). Allowed: hi = max(the provider's hi, cumulative), spent = hi - base, remaining = base + cap - hi, decimal strings
rules.recheck: spendRecheck(record, check): a later verifyMandate result against the started record. stop lists, in this order: spend-mandate-changed (the check's mandateHash is not the record's), spend-revoked (the check has mandate-revoked), spend-expired (mandate-expired), spend-consumer-changed (the check names a consumer, not the record's), spend-escrow-changed once (a pinned provider's scope reading names an escrow, not the pinned one; a reading without an escrow is no change). problems are the check's own problem codes, in order; when it has none, spend-not-enforced if the check's phase is not 1, its enforcement is not escrow-channel, or a record provider has no scope reading with both an escrow and a claimedAtCheck (review p1m4: a phase-0 result proves nothing about the channels). hi, per record provider in order: the larger of its hi and the claimedAtCheck the check read on the pinned escrow when the check names the record's consumer (a reading on another escrow, for another consumer or a check naming none, or no reading, leaves hi). ok when stop and problems are both empty and the check is ok
rules.resume: spendResume(record, request): may an order resume after a restart? record is the spend record of the order's agent key (null: none); request.key is the address the sealed key opens to, or "missing" (no sealed key in the store) or "unreadable" (the vault could not open it); request.mandateHash is the hash of the fresh check of the order's stored mandate (null: none). Refused with the first that applies, in this order: spend-state-lost (no record); spend-stopped (the record has stopped); spend-key-lost (key missing); spend-key-unreadable (key unreadable); spend-key-mismatch (request.chainId is not the record's, or request.agentKey or request.key is not the record's agentKey); spend-resume-mismatch (a started record and a mandateHash that is not the record's, or none; an accepted record and a mandateHash). Addresses and hashes compare in any case. Otherwise ok
rules.statement: spendStatement(record, check): the agent's spend statement from its started record and its last verifyMandate result before it signs the delivery. Empty when the check names no consumer or another consumer than the record's. Otherwise, per record provider in order, the entry { provider, escrow (the pinned ones), claimedAtStart (the provider's base), claimedAtDelivery (the check's claimedAtCheck for that provider), spent (claimedAtDelivery - claimedAtStart) }, decimal strings, when the check has a scope reading for the provider whose escrow is the pinned one and whose claimedAtCheck is a decimal string at least the base; no entry otherwise (an amount is never made up). Addresses compare in any case; the entry carries the record's
rules.evidence: spendEvidence(spend, { mandate, calls, readings, prices }): the deliver result's spend member reconciled. The capped providers are the mandate's scope items with a cap other than 0. Problems, in this order: spend-evidence-malformed when spend is not an array or has more entries than capped providers (then nothing else: no item, no warning); for each entry in order, spend-evidence-malformed when it is not an object with a provider address, an escrow address other than zero, and claimedAtStart, claimedAtDelivery and spent as decimal strings without leading zeros below 2^256, or when its provider was already named by an earlier well-formed entry; spend-provider-out-of-scope when its provider is not a capped provider; spend-evidence-inconsistent when claimedAtDelivery is below claimedAtStart or spent is not claimedAtDelivery - claimedAtStart. Every other entry is an item, in order, and gets its warnings in this order: spend-escrow-changed when readings has an entry for the provider with an escrow and a claimedAtCheck and that escrow is not the item's; otherwise, with such a reading on the same escrow, claimedNow is its claimedAtCheck, spentNow is claimedNow - claimedAtStart when claimedNow is at least claimedAtStart (else null), and spend-above-chain when claimedNow is below claimedAtDelivery; spend-above-cap when the measured amount (spentNow when not null, else spent) is above the provider's cap; then, when prices has a table for the provider (lower case) and every ok call to the provider (calls with ok true whose provider is it) has a method with a decimal-string price in it, expected is the sum of those prices and reconciled compares the measured amount (spentNow when not null, else spent) with it: equal, above (spend-exceeds-receipts) or below (spend-below-receipts); without such a table or with a call whose method has no price, expected and reconciled are null. Last, spend-evidence-incomplete for each capped provider, in scope order, that no entry names by a provider address (a malformed entry with an address names it). Addresses compare in any case. ok when there is no problem. expect lists the problem codes and the warning codes in order and, per item, reconciled, spentNow and expected
rules.keyVault: A key-vault blob is the string "tapeapi-key-vault:v1:" followed by lower-case hex of salt (16 bytes) || nonce (24 bytes) || ciphertext || tag (16 bytes), at least 56 bytes; anything else is key-vault-malformed. key = scrypt(UTF-8(passphrase), salt, N = 131072, r = 8, p = 1, 32 bytes). ciphertext || tag = XChaCha20-Poly1305(key, nonce, aad, plaintext), aad = UTF-8("tapeapi/key-vault/v1" LF context). Opening fails (key-vault-open-failed) when the tag does not verify with the key derived from the passphrase and the blob's salt, for the given context. The spend limiter seals an agent key's 32-byte secret for the context "tapeapi-spend-key/v1/<chainId>/<agentKey in lower case>". Each case gives key, the key derived from its passphrase and its blob's salt (null where the blob is malformed)
